key_bets: Energy confinement time scales as τₑ ~ R² in a D-He3 dipole at meter-scale radius, enabling Q > 1 at orbital device dimensions
He3 can be self-bred from D-D side reactions at rates sufficient to sustain commercial operation without external procurement
End-to-end power beaming efficiency (proton deceleration → DC → microwave transmitter → atmosphere → rectenna → AC grid) exceeds ~30% at multi-MW scale
Direct energy conversion of 14.7 MeV D-He3 protons achieves efficiency comparable to or better than 1970s Venetian blind DEC (50–65%) despite qualitatively different proton range physics
HTS REBCO coil can be space-qualified to survive Van Allen radiation, thermal cycling, and magnetic stress over a multi-year orbital lifetime with on-board cryocooler and radiator cooling
D-He3 plasma at 50–100 keV ion temperatures can be sustained in dipole geometry despite LDX/RT-1 having only demonstrated sub-fusion electron temperatures (few hundred eV)
Low-cost launch (Falcon 9 $2,700/kg trending to Starship $200/kg) keeps transport cost a small fraction of total CAPEX for a 5,000–15,000 kg spacecraft
eliminated_costs: Vacuum vessel (CAS 23) — space vacuum replaces the pumped chamber
Tritium breeding blanket (CAS 21) and associated Li-6 enrichment, FLiBe/Li-metal handling, and tritium processing infrastructure
Neutron shielding (CAS 22) — aneutronic D-He3 fuel eliminates W, WC cermet, and B₄C shielding supply chain
Thermal conversion cycle (CAS 24–26) — turbine plant, electrical plant, and heat rejection replaced by direct conversion + beaming
Reactor building and site civil construction — spacecraft replaces the terrestrial plant footprint
novel_costs: Launch cost to LEO as primary CAPEX driver (~$27M at Falcon 9 pricing for a 10,000 kg spacecraft)
Phased-array microwave transmitter fabrication (~$20M at ~2,500 kg and ~$2,000/kg for space-grade electronics) — the dominant novel hardware line item
Ground rectenna infrastructure for power beaming reception (~$2M/MW based on GW-class GEO SPS analogue)
He3 fuel procurement at ~$5,000–6,000/std L (~$28–34M/kg) market price, or self-breeding infrastructure as alternative
Space-qualified HTS coil system with on-board cryocooler, thermal radiators, and quench protection for a free-floating coil in LEO

risks.description: He3 fuel supply constraint — global production is ~1.8–2.7 kg/year; a MW-class plant would consume a rate comparable to total world production, and market-purchase at $30M/kg alone pushes LCOE to ~$1,446/MWh (>15× terrestrial fusion parity)

He3 self-breeding is categorically insufficient at equimolar D:He3 composition — D-D/D-He3 rate ratio is only ~7.5%, requiring a 13:1 D-rich fuel mix that restores neutron production and negates the aneutronic advantage

End-to-end power beaming efficiency is ~7–9% under realistic phased-array steering (transmitter DC-RF drops below 20% due to 4–6 dB phase shifter losses per element), well below the ~30% hypothesis and ~40% competitive threshold

Energy conversion pathway is completely unspecified by Zephyr — direct conversion of 14.7 MeV protons has no commercial supply chain, and the Venetian blind DEC efficiency figure is an optimistic upper bound from an inapplicable 1970s non-fusion-ion design basis

Energy confinement scaling law for dipole geometry is explicitly absent from the literature ("no such model exists for dipoles" — OpenStar study); τₑ ~ R² claim is unverified at fusion-relevant conditions
D-He3 confinement physics requires ion temperatures 2–3 orders of magnitude above LDX/RT-1 demonstrated conditions and a triple product ~10× higher than the D-T dipole reference

He3 procurement faces regulatory barriers independent of physical scarcity — He3 and tritium are dual-use controlled materials under DOE/DHS/DOD/NSS oversight with government-rationed allocation prioritizing security uses over commercial users

No heating specification disclosed — recirculating power fraction is a critical LCOE input that cannot be estimated; a high recirculating fraction could render an otherwise attractive concept non-viable
Orbital HTS coil radiation hardening, cryocooler thermal management, and multi-year lifetime in LEO are unvalidated — no space-qualified HTS cryocooler at fusion coil scale exists
Spacecraft fabrication cost for FOAK orbital fusion reactor could be 10–100× baseline, and the SPS parity window closes between 1.0× and 2.0× baseline hardware cost per sensitivity sweep
Orbital operations cost structure (debris mitigation for 10–50 m plasma radius, radiation hardening, no crewed EVA servicing, orbital lifetime management) has no precedent in fusion LCOE literature
Nuclear operations in orbit require IAEA oversight and international agreements with no established commercial precedent

NASA/DOE concluded GEO SPS is "not currently practical for power transmission to Earth" independent of launch cost — ground infrastructure scale was identified as a separate barrier applicable to Zephyr's beaming approach

Company is pre-prototype with ~2 employees, no technical papers, patents, or grants — entire technical disclosure fits on a single YC launch page, leaving all plasma parameters, Q, heating, conversion, and cost estimates undefined
